reference_vs_copy.title: Assignment creates a copy
reference_vs_copy.explanation: In Python, assigning one list to another variable does not create a new list. Both variables refer to the same list.

diagnostic.question: If a = [10, 20] and b = a, what happens to a when we execute b.append(30)?

transfer.question: Suppose d1 = {'x': 1} and d2 = d1. If d2['y'] = 2, what will d1 contain?

off_by_one.title: Loop boundary misunderstanding
off_by_one.explanation: Python's range() includes the starting value but excludes the ending value. This can cause a loop to execute a different number of times than expected.

transfer.question: Which values are produced by range(2, 6)?

print_vs_return.title: Confusing print() with return
print_vs_return.explanation: print() displays a value, while return sends a value back from a function so that it can be stored or used elsewhere.

example.code:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

result = add(2, 3)
print(result)

diagnostic.question: What does return do inside a function?
options: It displays the value on the screen
It sends a value back to the caller
